# rasuvaeff/yii3-outbox-db

Database-backed `StorageInterface` for `rasuvaeff/yii3-outbox` (yiisoft/db).

## Install

```bash
composer require rasuvaeff/yii3-outbox-db
```

## Rules

- `DbOutboxStorage implements Rasuvaeff\Yii3Outbox\RetryAwareStorageInterface`
  (which extends `StorageInterface`). Requires `rasuvaeff/yii3-outbox` ^1.5.
- `save()` upserts by `OutboxMessage::getId()` — the durable identity and the
  at-least-once dedup anchor; never regenerate it.
- `claim(array $types = [], int $limit = 1000)`: **what workers must use.**
  In one transaction: flips up to `$limit` `Pending` rows to `Processing` with a
  random `claimed_by` token and returns exactly those rows, `created_at` ASC.
  Concurrent workers never get the same message. Every claimed message must end
  in `markPublished()`, `markFailed()` or `save($msg->withStatus(Pending))`.
- `claimReady(DateTimeImmutable $readyThreshold, int $maxAttempts, array $types = [], int $limit = 1000)`:
  what `Processor` actually calls. Same claim plus
  `AND (attempts >= :maxAttempts OR last_attempt_at IS NULL OR last_attempt_at <= :readyThreshold)`,
  so a message still in backoff is never taken and never written back.
  The `attempts >= :maxAttempts` disjunct is mandatory: an exhausted message
  can only be marked `Failed`, and only if the claim returned it. No migration
  and no new index — `idx_<table>_pending` still narrows the scan; an `OR`
  across two columns is not indexable as a whole. `ProcessingResult::$skipped`
  therefore reads 0, and an exhausted message is failed up to `delaySeconds` later.
- `findPending(array $types = [], int $limit = 1000)`: read-only listing of
  `Pending` rows, optional type filter (empty = all), `created_at` ASC. No
  atomicity — two workers get the same rows. Dashboards only, never a worker.
- Type filter lets several consumers share one outbox; their type sets must not
  overlap, since `claim()` gives a message to exactly one caller.
- `markPublished`/`markFailed` re-save with the new status, preserving the
  attempt count / `last_attempt_at` of the passed message.
- `claim()` also stamps `claimed_at`; `save()` clears `claimed_by`/`claimed_at`.
- `findStaleClaims(DateTimeImmutable $claimedBefore, int $limit = 1000)` /
  `releaseStaleClaims(...)`: rows still `Processing` whose claim is older than
  the threshold (a `claimed_at` of NULL counts as stale), and putting them back
  to `Pending` without spending an attempt. This is the recovery path for a
  worker killed mid-batch — run it from cron with a threshold longer than the
  slowest batch.
- Migrations: `M260611000000CreateOutboxTable`, then
  `M260820000000AddOutboxClaimedAt` (adds `claimed_at` + processing index;
  `down()` is MySQL/PostgreSQL only, SQLite cannot drop a column).
- `payload` is `TEXT`: unbounded on PostgreSQL/SQLite, 65,535 bytes on MySQL.
  Not widened by a migration on purpose; `ALTER TABLE <your table> MODIFY
  payload MEDIUMTEXT NOT NULL` if your events need it (the table is
  `table_prefix` + `table` from params, `outbox` by default). Over the limit:
  MySQL strict mode fails the insert and takes the business transaction with it;
  a permissive mode truncates silently and publishes the remains.
- `DbOutboxStorage` takes an optional `Psr\Clock\ClockInterface` (used for
  `claimed_at`); without one it reads the system clock in UTC.
- Datetimes stored as `Y-m-d H:i:s` UTC strings.
- Corrupt rows → `InvalidOutboxRowException` (never silently coerced).
- Core `yii3-outbox` ships no `config/di.php`; this backend (or the app) is the
  single source of `StorageInterface`.

## API

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Outbox\Outbox;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Outbox\OutboxStatus;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3OutboxDb\DbOutboxStorage;

$storage = new DbOutboxStorage(db: $connection, table: 'outbox');

$outbox = new Outbox(storage: $storage, clock: $clock);
$outbox->record(type: 'ab.exposure', payload: '{"experiment":"checkout"}');

$claimed = $storage->claim(types: ['ab.exposure'], limit: 1000);  // workers
$ready   = $storage->claimReady($policy->readyThreshold($now), 3, ['ab.exposure']); // what Processor uses
$pending = $storage->findPending(types: ['ab.exposure'], limit: 1000); // read-only
$storage->markPublished($message);
$storage->markFailed($message);
$message = $storage->getById($id);          // ?OutboxMessage
$purged  = $storage->deleteByStatus(OutboxStatus::Published);
```

## Migration

Classes: `Rasuvaeff\Yii3OutboxDb\Migration\M260611000000CreateOutboxTable`,
then `Rasuvaeff\Yii3OutboxDb\Migration\M260820000000AddOutboxClaimedAt`
(namespaced since 2.0). Register BY NAMESPACE:

```php
MigrationService::class => [
    'setSourceNamespaces()' => [['App\\Migration', 'Rasuvaeff\\Yii3OutboxDb\\Migration']],
],
```

Table name: params only (`table_prefix` + `table`) => `OutboxTableName` (VO) =>
both the storage and the migration. Configuring the migration through the
container does NOT work (Injector::make() resolves by type, not by class-id):
such a definition is inert, not fatal. `setSourceNamespaces()` above is the
supported DI entry point.

Columns: `id` (PK), `type`, `payload`, `status`, `created_at`, `attempts`,
`last_attempt_at`, `aggregate_id`, `claimed_by`, `claimed_at`. Index
`idx_<table>_pending` backs the pending poll; `idx_<table>_processing`
(`status`, `claimed_at`) backs stale-claim recovery.

`M260820000000AddOutboxClaimedAt` is mandatory: `claim()` writes `claimed_at`,
so run `migrate:up` BEFORE deploying the new code. `down()` is MySQL/PostgreSQL
only — `yiisoft/db-sqlite` cannot drop a column.

## DI / params

```php
// config/params.php
'rasuvaeff/yii3-outbox-db' => ['table' => 'outbox'],
```

Binds `StorageInterface => DbOutboxStorage` from `config/di.php`.
